column1: # Second-reader exemption registry -- a ratchet, never an escape hatch.
# Format: <card id> TAB <reason>.
# count: 2 entry(ies) across 2 card(s)
# `.board/validate.sh` derives that number from the entries below and requires
# `.board/README.md` to carry the identical sentence. No other line here may
# count anything.
# The second reader is reachable only through a concrete
# Unit/Contract/Integration/E2E citation. A card whose four layers all read
# `not-applicable: <reason>` therefore never touched it, and until this registry
# existed that absence was silent: the card simply skipped the gate and nothing
# in the board said so. Two cards sat in `done` in exactly that shape, one of
# them justifying itself with "o comportamento e local e coberto pelo
# acceptance" -- covered, that is, by the single engine this gate exists to
# distrust.
# So the absence is named instead of hidden, and it is printed on every
# validate.sh run as `board note:`. The registry only shrinks:
# `.board/validate.sh` refuses an entry for a card that is not in `done`, for a
# card that has since started citing a concrete layer test, and for any card
# outside the frozen set compiled into `.board/validate.sh`. A card entering
# `review` or `done` from now on cannot be added -- it must hand the second
# reader something it can execute.
AUR-016
column2: All four TDD layers are not-applicable, so no artifact exists for either second-reader engine to run; the delivered artifact is the ISO 25010 policy table and only the acceptance program reads it, which is one engine deciding alone.
